Even though Mac shipments in Q3 2026 dropped 11%, according to the latest IDC report, as the overall market shipments plummeted 20.1%, Apple's market share still rose from 8.5% to 9.5%. Below are the details.

In a challenging environment, Apple still performed better than most of the PC market

IDC today released its Q3 2026 global PC shipment report, noting that although Mac shipments declined compared to the same period last year, Apple clearly outperformed the overall market.

According to IDC's preliminary data, Apple shipped a total of 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million units in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market saw an even more significant decline, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-on-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

This performance keeps Apple firmly in fourth place. The top three in order are: market leader Lenovo with 14.9 million units shipped and a market share of 23.8%; HP with 10.3 million units shipped and a market share of 16.5%; Dell with 7.6 million units shipped and a market share of 12.1%.

Among the top five brands, HP saw the largest year-on-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS had the smallest decline, falling 8.6% year-on-year, shipping 5.5 million units for a market share of 8.7%.

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "channel concerns about weak demand amid high inventory and high prices could trigger promotional activity in the near term," adding that "prices will remain well above last year's levels."

The firm also said that the economy has weakened since last quarter, which could further hurt demand, making "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027 even gloomier."
